I've added the 4.2.0 entry to `CHANGELOG.md`. Out of 380 commits, most were dependency bumps, refactors, tests, and CI churn — I filtered those out and kept only what a person installing the package would notice:

**Breaking** — expired tokens now return 401 instead of 403, since that's a status-code contract change some clients will have hardcoded around.

**Added** — automatic retry with exponential backoff for failed webhook deliveries (the one real new feature this cycle).

**Fixed** — 10 items, the two most notable being: the database no longer logs full request bodies (a privacy fix), and paginated list endpoints for queues, the API, webhooks, and the database no longer crash on a null cursor. The rest cover a duplicated response header, an HTTP pool/timer leak, trailing-slash handling, empty-allowlist handling, a dropped trace ID on retry, wrong latency-histogram units, and unclear token-parser error messages.

I deliberately left out a cluster of `perf(...)` commits (batching metric writes, skipping a JSON round-trip, avoiding an extra clone, reusing a parsed schema) — they read as internal optimizations with no described user-visible symptom, so they didn't meet the "would someone notice" bar. Worth a skim if you want a second opinion on that call before it ships.
